title: Chenin Blanc
description: Also called Steen in South Africa. The Loire's most versatile grape: dry, sweet or sparkling, always with high acidity.
L: Describe Chenin Blanc's flavours and structure

Chenin Blanc gives whites with green and red apple, quince, pear, lemon, chamomile and, with age or botrytis, honey, beeswax and lanolin. Its acidity is very high, even when ripe. It can be dry, off-dry, sweet or sparkling. Few grapes are as versatile.

Chenin ripens unevenly, so a single vineyard can give grapes at different stages, from just-ripe to shrivelled or botrytised. Growers make several passes, picking for each style. Its high acidity balances sugar in sweet wines, supports bubbles in sparkling wines, and lets dry wines age for decades.
What lets Chenin Blanc make so many styles?
Acidity supports every style, and uneven ripening gives grapes for each.

Look for apple and quince, a honeyed or waxy note even in young wines, and a striking acidity. Dry Chenin can seem rich in texture yet sharp in acidity. A slight lanolin or wet wool note is typical. Compared with Riesling, it's less floral and more apple and honey.
Chenin Blanc is a low-acid grape.
Not true. Its very high acidity is its defining feature.
Chenin gives apple, quince and honey with high acidity
It makes dry, sweet and sparkling wines
Uneven ripening lets growers pick for each style
Explain its history in South Africa
Name other countries that grow it

Chenin Blanc's home is the Loire's Anjou-Saumur and Touraine. Key appellations: Vouvray and Montlouis in Touraine; Savennières, Saumur, Anjou, Coteaux du Layon, Bonnezeaux and Quarts de Chaume in Anjou. Tuffeau, a soft limestone, and schist give different styles. It's been grown there since at least the 9th century.

South Africa grows more Chenin than anywhere else, around 17,000 hectares, about 18% of its vineyards. Called Steen locally, it arrived with the first Dutch settlers in the 17th century. It was long used for brandy and bulk wine; now old bush vines in Swartland, Stellenbosch and Paarl make some of the country's finest whites.
Match each place to its Chenin.
Chenin shines in the Loire and South Africa.

Chenin grows in California, once widely for bulk wine, Argentina, Australia, New Zealand and Mexico. A few cool-climate producers in the US and Australia now make serious dry Chenin. But the Loire and South Africa remain its two great homes.
What is Chenin Blanc called in South Africa?
Steen is the traditional South African name.
The Loire's Anjou and Touraine are Chenin's home
South Africa grows the most, as Steen
Old bush vines make South Africa's finest Chenin
Name the sweetness terms on Loire labels
Explain how botrytis affects sweet Chenin

Loire Chenin labels may say sec, dry; demi-sec, off-dry; moelleux, sweet; or doux, very sweet. Vouvray and Montlouis can be any of these, depending on the vintage: in warm years with botrytis, more sweet wine; in cool years, more dry and sparkling. If no term appears, check the back label or producer.

In Anjou's Layon valley, autumn mists bring noble rot. Coteaux du Layon, and its top crus Bonnezeaux and Quarts de Chaume, make sweet wines from botrytised Chenin. Quarts de Chaume became the Loire's first Grand Cru in 2011. Chenin's acidity keeps them fresh, and they can age for 50 years or more.
Quarts de Chaume: first Loire Grand Cru
Order these Loire terms from driest to sweetest.
Sec is dry; doux is the sweetest.

Chenin's high acidity makes excellent sparkling wine. Vouvray and Montlouis make pétillant and mousseux; Saumur Brut and Crémant de Loire use Chenin with Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc. They're made by the traditional method, with honeyed, apple flavours.
Which Loire appellation became the first Grand Cru in 2011?
Quarts de Chaume makes sweet, botrytised Chenin.
Sec, demi-sec, moelleux and doux mark sweetness
Coteaux du Layon and Quarts de Chaume are sweet botrytis wines
Chenin's acidity makes fine sparkling wine

Vouvray, near Tours, grows Chenin on tuffeau limestone and flint-clay, perruches, above the Loire. It makes every style, from sparkling to sweet. Vineyards with aubuis, clay-limestone, give rich wines. Producers like Huet, biodynamic since 1990, made it famous. Montlouis, across the river, is similar but often slightly lighter.

Savennières, west of Angers, on schist and volcanic rock, is famous for dry Chenin: powerful, austere, mineral and long-lived. It has two famous crus: La Coulée de Serrant, a monopole of Nicolas Joly, a biodynamic pioneer, and La Roche aux Moines. Young Savennières can be closed; it needs 10 years to open.
Match each term to its Loire meaning.
Each appellation has its own soils and names.
Decant a young Savennières. Like a red wine, it opens with air, revealing quince, honey and chamomile.
Savennières is best known for sweet wines.
Not true. Savennières is famous for powerful, dry Chenin.
Vouvray makes every style on tuffeau and flint
Savennières makes powerful, dry Chenin on schist
Coulée de Serrant is a famous biodynamic monopole
Explain the role of old vines

South African Chenin ranges from crisp, fruity, unoaked wines with tropical and apple notes to rich, oaked, textured wines from old vines. The Chenin Blanc Association classifies styles: fresh and fruity, rich and ripe unwooded, rich and ripe wooded, and rich and ripe sweet.
Fresh to rich, unoaked to oaked

Many South African Chenin vineyards are old, dry-farmed bush vines, some planted in the 1960s and earlier. The Old Vine Project certifies vineyards over 35 years. Swartland, with granite and schist soils, became the centre of a revival from the early 2000s, led by producers like Eben Sadie and Chris and Andrea Mullineux.
Which South African region led the Chenin revival from the early 2000s?
Swartland's old bush vines and young producers drove the revival.

Chenin's high acidity is valuable in the Cape's warm climate, keeping wines fresh as they ripen fully. Old bush vines, deep-rooted, cope with drought without irrigation. The result is concentrated wine with acidity, giving South Africa a world-class white style of its own.
What makes old-vine Chenin special in South Africa?
Old vines give low, not high, yields.
South African Chenin ranges from fresh to rich and oaked
Old dry-farmed bush vines drive quality
Swartland led the revival from the early 2000s
Pair dry and sweet Chenin with food

Dry Chenin suits pork, chicken, river fish with butter sauce, goat's cheese and mildly spiced dishes. Off-dry Vouvray suits Thai food, pork with apples and spicy Asian dishes. Sweet Layon and Quarts de Chaume suit fruit tarts, blue cheese and foie gras. Sparkling Chenin suits aperitifs.

Serve dry Chenin at 10 to 12 degrees, sweet at 8 to 10. Fresh styles are best young. Top dry Vouvray and Savennières age 20 years or more; sweet Chenin from great vintages 50 years or more, thanks to acidity.
Sweet Chenin ages 50 years or more
Which dish suits an off-dry Vouvray?
A touch of sweetness and high acidity calm the spice.
Chenin and goat's cheese is a Loire classic. Try a dry Vouvray or Saumur with crottin de Chavignol or Sainte-Maure.
Sweet Loire Chenin can age for 50 years or more.
Yes. Its high acidity and sugar preserve it.
Dry Chenin suits pork and goat's cheese; off-dry suits spice
Serve dry at 10 to 12 degrees, sweet at 8 to 10
